title: Coinbase blocks $4.7 million in transfers to Elon Musk deepfake scam
content_md: Coinbase says it blocked $4.7 million in cryptocurrency transfers to scammers promoting a fake giveaway using an AI-generated deepfake of Elon Musk during a Tesla livestream that attracted more than 500,000 viewers. The deepfake took place during Tesla's "flying car" demonstration, when scammers created a fake YouTube livestream that appeared to broadcast the event. The fraudulent stream featured an AI-generated video of Musk, cryptocurrency wallet addresses, and a QR code, promising viewers that any cryptocurrency they sent would be doubled. According to Coinbase, hundreds of its customers attempted to send millions of dollars to the scammers over about two hours, including many longtime users of the exchange. However, the company says its AI-powered fraud-prevention systems detected the scam and blocked about 91% of the attempted transfers, totaling $4.7 million. Unlike traditional cryptocurrency theft involving compromised accounts or stolen credentials, victims in this campaign voluntarily made the crypto transfer after believing the livestream was real. Coinbase explained that this makes scams like these difficult to detect because the transactions are created and approved by legitimate account holders. "Most fraud defenses are built to spot activity the customer didn't authorize," Coinbase explained . "That's not what happened here.
